findings.title: R10_VALIDATION section 8 says J440's four tails are not in the tail allocation and it was not re-run; the fit checker allocates all 27 tails, J440's included, on every run
findings.contradicts: docs/R10_VEHICLE_HANDOFF.md line 84: 'The fit checker separately allocates all 27 solder tails to their native pad XY boxes'; tools/fit_check.py lines 446-454 (profile r10 adds a tail box for every PTH pad of every M3_DB125_* footprint, so J440 is included automatically); tools/check.sh line 59 runs fit_check --profile r10 on every gate run.
findings.evidence: docs/R10_VALIDATION.md line 2923-2928, in the current owner section 'R10 deviations for owner acceptance' / '8. Mechanics, access and retention': 'all 23 tails of the seven earlier terminals have separate fit allocations ... Minimum tail/bore clearance 7.558359 mm ... J440's four tails were not added to that tail allocation (not re-run).' Run on a0ec075e: KiCad python -I -B tools/fit_check.py m3_design/assembly_review/m3.kicad_pcb --profile r10 --report .supervisor/r29_mechanics/fit.json -> terminal_tails.count = 27, minimum_bore_margin_mm = 7.5583593625; rows 'J440.1 terminal tail' ... 'J440.4 terminal tail' present (x 6.45-8.35, y 10.05-22.45, z -3.80..-1.60, margin 7.558 mm each). The sentence and the handoff's '27 solder tails' were written in the same commit (6628488, round 19), when fit_check already had this generic DB125 tail loop (unchanged since), so J440's tails have been allocated and re-checked on every board since 50a39de5. The recorded minimum 7.558359 mm is unchanged with them.
findings.impact: The owner list tells the owner that J440's solder tails have no fit allocation, which is false and contradicts the handoff; no physical consequence (the J440 tails clear by 7.558 mm, as the other 23).
findings.concrete_fix: Text only, R10_VALIDATION line 2923-2928: 'all 27 tails of the eight terminals (J440 included since 50a39de5) have separate fit allocations ... Minimum tail/bore clearance 7.558359 mm (unchanged on a0ec075e)'; delete 'J440's four tails were not added to that tail allocation (not re-run).'

observations: Plate model re-run on a0ec075e (tools/plate_model.py --profile r10, masses.json): 180.8 / 255.6 Hz pinned D5 / D10, 287.8 / 407.0 Hz clamped, 78.6 g, max 100 g deflection 1.27 mm at (46,44.5); 0.5 mm raster gaps at 4 mm standoffs C431 0.261, C421 0.320, C411 0.558, L1 0.524 mm; contact onset C431 125 (250) g, C421 133 (265) g, C411 175 (350.5) g, L1 214 (428) g; all match ORDERING 8.4 and the handoff.

The records say the plate model was 'not re-run on 1407e850, 92c3ad59 or a0ec075e', but review probes (r24 to r28 mechanics, and this round) re-ran it with identical figures; the records describe their own provenance and the figures hold, so not counted.

The 256.1 / 287.9 / 407.1 Hz and 1.24 mm figures quoted in M3_R10 'Current mechanical integration' and R10_VALIDATION section 8 are labelled as 632a9ad3 figures; the current board gives 255.6 / 287.8 / 407.0 Hz and 1.27 mm (labelled to their board; judged in round 28).
J9 / J420 tail allocations reach a 4 mm sled at 162-176 g (D5), before C411 and L1; they lie in the x 31.5-41 / y 20-60 pocket window (already ruled in rounds 25 / 26).
C128 strain 991 microstrain at 100 g reproduced (R10_VALIDATION row 1); C431 1221, J410 1421, J420 1414, J9 1313, J400 1157 (row 11's 1.2-1.4 millistrain holds).
Nut-inclusive h + t limits recomputed: 6.018 mm at x 4 / 42 and 5.365 mm at x 3.7 (stated as < 6.0 and < 5.3, conservative).

The 'C23 courtyard gap 0.575 mm' in R10_VALIDATION section 8 is J430's closed fit envelope (y 34.0) to C23's courtyard (y 34.575); the courtyard-to-courtyard gap is 0.45 mm. The sentence is about the closed allocation, so not counted.
J3's courtyard 1.67 mm from J440 is the courtyard line-centre gap (23.675 to 25.345); polygon edge gap 1.73 mm.
